data.title: Nvidia and Micron: AI Slowdown Will Punish One AI Stock More Than the Other, Says Investor
data.description:
Calls to slow the pace of frontier AI development put the semiconductor sector back on edge on Monday. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei recently argued that the industry should "pace the frontier" to give companies more time for safety testing, oversight and governance, with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and other AI leaders generally supportive of the idea. The market reaction was immediate, with several semiconductor stocks selling off sharply as investors questioned whether slower model development could eventually mean less spending on AI infrastructure.

But slowing the development of ever-more-powerful models does not necessarily mean slowing AI infrastructure demand. The bigger shift may be from training the next frontier model toward running AI at enormous scale. As inference costs fall, companies can afford to use AI for more tasks, while agentic systems can generate huge numbers of tokens through repeated reasoning, planning and execution. That changes what matters in the semiconductor supply chain.

An investor with the moniker Summit Research (SR) argues that this distinction is particularly important when comparing Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Micron (NASDAQ:MU). Both benefit from AI spending, but their exposure is different, leaving Nvidia more vulnerable if the industry places less emphasis on rapid frontier upgrades.

For Nvidia, the problem is not that demand for compute disappears. Inference should remain a huge source of demand. The issue is that a slower frontier could reduce the urgency to buy Nvidia's newest and most powerful accelerators. If AI labs take an extra year or two between major model advances, customers may have less reason to rush into each new generation of hardware.

That matters because Nvidia has built its business around a rapid upgrade cycle. Each generation promises substantial gains in performance and efficiency, allowing the company to sell customers more powerful systems and support premium pricing. If frontier progress slows, however, the monetization of that annual cadence could become less predictable. Customers may continue buying Nvidia hardware, but they could put greater emphasis on cost-effective inference rather than paying up for maximum performance.

There is also a potential margin issue. Nvidia has argued that technological leadership and major performance-per-dollar improvements are central to sustaining its gross margins. A shift toward cheaper, inference-focused systems could therefore create a less favourable product mix, particularly if customers become less willing to pay for the very latest hardware.

Micron has a different exposure. Its HBM is tied closely to Nvidia and other AI accelerators, so a slowdown in frontier upgrades would still create some risk. But Micron also supplies server DRAM and NAND storage, areas that can benefit directly from the sheer volume of AI workloads.

Agentic AI requires large amounts of memory and storage to handle expanding context windows, KV caches and persistent data. That means Micron can benefit even when the AI industry is running more workloads on existing or less cutting-edge accelerators. Its opportunity is therefore tied more closely to the number of tokens being processed than to how quickly the frontier model itself advances.

SR also points to a crucial supply constraint. Micron has indicated that its HBM capacity is already accounted for well into 2028, while conventional DRAM is also facing tight supply. If frontier demand softens, capacity could potentially be redirected toward other memory products needed for large-scale inference.

That gives Micron a wider cushion. Nvidia remains heavily exposed to the pace of its accelerator upgrade cycle, while Micron can participate across several layers of the AI memory hierarchy.

As such, SR has downgraded Nvidia's rating to Hold (i.e., Neutral), while the investor maintained a Buy rating for Micron. (To watch Summit Research's track record, click here)

On the other hand, the Street has a bullish stance for both names, giving the pair Strong Buy consensus ratings. At $324.30, NVDA's average price target points toward 12-month returns of 54%. Micron's average target stands at $1,563.93, a figure offering one-year upside of 69%. (See Nvidia stock forecast or Micron stock forecast)

data.title: Stock Market Today, September 15 – Futures Slip as Treasury Yields Cross 5%, Rate Hike Looms
data.description:
U.S. stock futures fell ahead of Tuesday's session as surging oil prices fueled renewed inflation concerns, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.03%. Investors are awaiting the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on Wednesday. Markets are pricing in a 92% probability of a 0.25 percentage-point rate hike, which would raise the Fed's benchmark interest rate to 3.75%-4.00%.

Futures on the Nasdaq 100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were down 0.63%, 0.55%, and 0.67%, respectively, as of 5:38 a.m. EDT on September 15.

Oil prices extended gains on Tuesday as fresh attacks in the Gulf raised concerns about supply disruptions. Saudi Arabia also shut its key East-West oil pipeline, which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, after drone attacks damaged it, further tightening supply. At the time of writing, Brent crude (CM:BZ) rose to $108.88 a barrel, while WTI crude (CM:CL) was near $104.03 a barrel.

data.title: JPM Benefits from Higher Rates, but Earnings Growth Is Slowing
data.description:
JPMorgan Chase (JPM) is benefiting from higher rates, but earnings growth is slowing. Shares of the largest U.S. bank have outperformed the broader U.S. financials sector in 2026, as measured by popular ETFs such as the iShares U.S. Financials ETF (IYF). JPMorgan Chase, the world's largest bank by market share, is set to deliver earnings growth of about 21% in 2026, driven by strong performance in businesses benefiting from robust capital markets activity.

Looking ahead to 2027, analysts expect JPMorgan Chase to grow earnings per share (EPS) by only about 3%. I expect the benefits from higher interest rates to be somewhat offset by a normalization in asset management and investment banking performance.

Coupled with a premium valuation of 14.7x 2026 earnings, especially relative to U.S. banking peers, I believe this dynamic supports a Hold rating for JPMorgan Chase, somewhat more bearish than the Moderate Buy Wall Street consensus rating.

data.title: Why Are Tech Stocks GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN Falling in Premarket Today, Sept. 15?
data.description:
U.S. tech giants Alphabet (GOOGL), Microsoft (MSFT), and Amazon (AMZN) are down in premarket trading today. The move comes as U.S. Treasury yields climbed to their highest level since 2007 and remain above 5%. Investors are worried that oil prices staying above $100 could add to inflation and put more pressure on the economy. GOOGL and MSFT stock are down by 1%, while AMZN fell 0.50% as of this writing.

Traders are also turning their attention to the Federal Reserve and are expecting a quarter-point rate hike. The Federal Reserve's two-day September meeting starts Tuesday.

What Higher Yields Mean for Tech Stocks

Higher government bond yields can increase borrowing costs for consumers and businesses while making stocks less attractive compared with bonds. This can put pressure on high-growth tech stocks such as Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon. Higher yields can also reduce the value investors place on future earnings, which may weigh on stock valuations.

data.title: Musk Leaves Door Open to Tesla-SpaceX Merger as TSLA, SPCX Stocks Fall
data.description:
Elon Musk has given investors his clearest signal yet that he is open to combining Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX), though he stopped short of confirming that merger talks are underway.

Speaking at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles on Monday, Musk was asked why Tesla and SpaceX remain separate despite growing cooperation between the two companies. He called it a "great question" and pointed to their expanding ties across several areas.

"With all this collaboration, on so many levels, who can imagine what action one might take when there's so much close collaboration in so many areas," Musk said. He did not give a timeline, deal structure, or commitment.

data.title: Citi Warns AI Safety Risks Could Threaten Stock Rally; Flags AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT
data.description:
Citigroup's head of U.S. equity trading strategy, Stuart Kaiser, warned that growing AI safety concerns could slow AI model development and weigh on corporate earnings, potentially putting pressure on U.S. stocks. Kaiser adopted a more cautious stance on equities, warning that slower AI progress could "crimp" earnings-per-share (EPS) revisions and weaken an important pillar of the market rally.

Citi also highlighted rising bond yields, surging oil prices, and the upcoming November midterm elections as potential headwinds for stocks. Citigroup expects the S&P 500 (SPX) to remain near its recent highs, although a 3%-5% pullback could attract buyers. Kaiser identified Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOGL), Meta (META), and Amazon (AMZN) as stocks that could be sensitive to these risks.

What Are the Key Headwinds for Stocks?

Here's how the three potential headwinds could impact the stock market:

Promotion

  • Rising bond yields: Higher yields can make bonds more attractive relative to stocks and put pressure on equity valuations, particularly high-growth stocks such as tech and AI.
  • Surging oil prices: Higher oil prices can fuel inflation, potentially increasing the chances of higher interest rates and squeezing corporate profit margins.
  • November midterm elections: Kaiser and his team believe Republicans could lose control of the House and Senate, potentially increasing market volatility. Companies tied to power generation and data centers could be particularly sensitive to potential policy changes.

Why Is Citi Growing Cautious on Stocks?

Kaiser noted that the S&P 500 fell 0.8% last week as investors focused on macroeconomic risks without the support of fresh earnings catalysts. He expects a challenging period ahead, citing a seasonally weak September and a higher bar for investors to re-engage with equities.

The bank expects the S&P 500 to remain within about 2% of its August highs, potentially keeping investors on the sidelines. A 3%-5% pullback could attract dip buyers, but the market may need to retest its all-time highs to trigger stronger buying.

Citi also warned that AI safety concerns could broadly weigh on investor sentiment, adding another layer of uncertainty for technology stocks.

AI Regulation in Focus

The AI safety debate intensified over the weekend after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slowdown in AI development. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman also dismissed the possibility of a 2026 IPO, while Elon Musk raised concerns about AI risks.

President Donald Trump, however, has opposed slowing AI development or imposing heavy regulation, arguing that the U.S. needs to maintain its technological advantage over China. He has dismissed some AI risk concerns as exaggerated while acknowledging that safeguards may still be needed.

data.title: President Trump Calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Live Onstage to Dismiss AI Safety Fears as a Hoax; NVDA Stock Drops 3.4%
data.description:
President Donald Trump phoned Nvidia (NVDA) Chief Executive Jensen Huang live on stage on Monday. Speaking to a room of tech investors at the All-In Summit, Trump told the crowd that fear over artificial intelligence is a hoax. Huang was in the middle of an on-stage talk when his phone rang. He placed the president on speakerphone so the audience could hear Trump's view on the tech market.

Trump argued that building large data centers brings great wealth to people and states. He noted that stopping AI work would play right into the hands of China. Huang agreed with the president during the call, stating that American firms will not let that happen. The phone call came after Trump posted on social media that strong leadership is the main safety tool the country needs, brushing off calls for strict government rules.

OpenAI and Anthropic Aim to Slowdown AI Model Updates

Nvidia shares fell despite the supportive words from the White House. Nvidia stock (NVDA) dropped nearly 3.4% on Monday afternoon to trade near $211.81. Other chipmakers took harder hits. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) slipped over 5%, while Intel (INTC) lost more than 5%. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX), a main fund tracking the chip sector, slid 6% as investors reacted to news from tech leaders.

The market drop started after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman supported calls to slow down AI model development to test safety. Traders grew worried that a pause by major AI labs could mean smaller chip orders. Still, some investors noted that the sell-off might be short-term panic rather than a real drop in chip demand.

Nvidia Maintains Strong Revenue Streams

Even if big AI labs slow down their work, Nvidia maintains strong revenue backup. Unlike competitors that count on a few big buyers, Nvidia sells hardware to a wide range of growing startups and software groups. Nvidia recently signed a $12.9 billion deal to buy Hugging Face, a major open-source software platform. This purchase keeps millions of developers using Nvidia chips even if giant labs cut spending.

At the same time, new projects continue to drive long-term chip orders. SpaceX (SPCX) chief Elon Musk confirmed that SpaceX plans to launch AI data centers into space next year using Nvidia chips. Building space data centers helps bypass land and power limits on Earth.
